nodes.title: STT spend is reported by the client and priced by the server. D4 transcription runs browser ↔ Azure over WebRTC, so the server only mints the token and never sees the session close. B Voice's cascade link emits one `stt.session {model, sec}` trace event per torn-down transcription call (close, reconnect, lane fallback), through the lesson's trace bus, and never a usd. server/cost/rollup.js always prices stt.session itself from {model, sec}, capped at 4 h per event, so a client can neither inflate nor zero the ledger. We chose this over estimating from lesson length × D4 share because it measures. Reverse if the client and the Cost Management STT meter disagree by more than 20% over a day (scripts/cost.mjs --reconcile): then estimate server-side instead.

tests/graceful-shutdown.test.mjs raced on a loaded CI runner: 'a request still open after the grace is cut' expected leftOpen 1 and got 0 once on PR #38 (C2 Games' report). The test slept a fixed 50 ms after sending a never-answered request, so the server had not accepted it yet when the drain ran. Both drain tests now poll requests.active() until the request is in flight, up to 5 s (Games' patch 001). Checked 3/3 green, then 3/3 green with six busy-loop processes on the 4-core container. The other new platform suites (ops, release, cost, shard, migrate) have no fixed sleeps.
